g.text: First-principles map: Authentication (AuthN), Authorization (AuthZ), Transport Encryption (mTLS), and Federation (SAML vs OIDC)
Unified Enterprise Architecture Flow: How Protocols Interact in Production
End-to-end request from client login to API gateway, microservice token exchange, and persistence
Architectural Cheat Sheet: Core Protocol Decisions at a Glance
SAML 2.0 = Heavy XML, enterprise browser SSO (Okta, Workday). OIDC = Lightweight JSON/JWT, built for mobile apps, SPAs & REST APIs.
OAuth 2.0 is Authorization ONLY (delegated access token). OIDC adds the Identity layer on top (OIDC = OAuth 2.0 + ID Token).
One-way TLS authenticates server only. Mutual TLS (mTLS) cryptographically verifies both client & server certificates at Layer 4.
JWT is stateless & verified locally (zero DB lookup). Opaque is a reference UUID (instant revocation, requires DB/Redis lookup per call).
